chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slaughtered meat of the People of the Book and their women, so he said: There is no harm in it.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of the People of the Book permissible for Shia Muslims to eat?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirming the permissibility (*la ba'sa bihi*) of consuming the meat of the People of the Book, a ruling foundational to Shia dietary jurisprudence. This hadith is frequently cited in discussions regarding the specific conditions of slaughter and the broader theological inclusion of Jews and Christians as 'People of the Book' in contrast to polytheists. It underscores the practical application of Quranic allowances, reinforcing the view that their ritual slaughter is valid for Shia consumption.
